claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Section heading printed in the PDF is transcribed as a plain paragraph with no Markdown heading marker, so it is lost from the document outline; should be '## 7.3 DIVISION, SECTION, PARAGRAPH FORMATS' (siblings such as 7.2.4 / 7.2 carry headings).

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 189 (folio IV-43) shows '7.3 DIVISION, SECTION, PARAGRAPH FORMATS' as a numbered clause heading, styled like its siblings 7.2.5 and 7.4. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md (and page-189.md) the line is a plain paragraph with no '#' marker, while the same chapter's siblings carry markers: '## 7.2 REFERENCE FORMAT REPRESENTATION', '### 7.2.1'..'### 7.2.4', '## 7.5 DECLARATIVES', '## 7.6 END PROGRAM HEADER'. The text matches, so the claim quotes both sources correctly, but the heading is lost from the outline. That is a real structural defect. The fix is '## 7.3 ...' to match '## 7.2' and '## 7.5'. Every other clause heading on this page (7.2.5, 7.3.1, 7.3.2, 7.3.3, 7.4) also lacks a marker, and this claim does not cover them.
